Marijampole New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Marijampolės apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. This is the newer of Marijampolė's two Jewish cemeteries. Jews likely settled in Marijampolė from the early 18th century, reaching 3,268 people (48 percent) by 1897. The town's Hebrew high school, opened in 1919, was the first of its kind anywhere in the Diaspora; among its former students was Baruch Ben Yehuda (1894–1990), who went on to serve as the first director general of Israel's Ministry of Education. After the 1941 German invasion, Jews were confined in the synagogue precinct, abused, and forced into labor before being shot on September 1, along with thousands of Jews from neighboring towns.
